saints.name: St. Zita
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A humble maidservant of Lucca who made a lifetime of housework a path to holiness…
biography: Born about 1212 to a poor family of Monsagrati, a village near Lucca, Zita entered at twelve the service of the Fatinelli, a prosperous household of that city, and remained their servant for some forty-eight years, sanctifying housework by prayer and by quiet gifts of food to the poor.

Her exactness at first earned only the jealousy of the other servants, whose accusations turned her employers against her, but her patient goodness outlasted their malice, and in time she was set over the whole household — generous in almsgiving, yet careful to relieve only genuine need.

She died at Lucca on 27 April 1272, in her sixtieth year, and miracles at her intercession made her so dear that Dante could style Lucca simply 'Santa Zita'. Her tomb in San Frediano was opened in 1580, and Innocent XII confirmed her cult in 1696. Because she spent her life as a maidservant, she is the patroness of domestic workers.
saints.knownFor: Sanctifying humble domestic service through charity and prayer.

canonization.canonized: Cult confirmed 1696 by Pope Innocent XII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 April
